A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same causality-guided debiasing framework and share substantial experimental material. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-D support comparison despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original WinoBias and Discrim-Eval experiments, human annotation outcomes, error analyses and prompting ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a BBQ evaluation and a Claude 2 prompting-strategy ablation.

M1.justification: The proposed causal model adds scenario as an input to historical selection S, and Strategy II now targets scenario as well as entity associations. The described WinoBias prompting sequence remains unchanged under DDP, the new name for Reduce + Fact.

E1.justification: v2 adds disambiguated BBQ question answering across nine social categories, extending coverage to disability, nationality, physical appearance, religion, socioeconomic status and sexual orientation. WinoBias and Discrim-Eval remain; moving Discrim-Eval into Appendix D.2 does not remove its coverage.

E2.justification: Matched WinoBias experiments retain Default, zero-shot COT and ICL. Discrim-Eval retains Illegal, Ignore, Really (4x), and Illegal + Ignore. BBQ evaluates the existing Default and ICL approaches; its eight-shot configuration changes settings rather than introducing a new comparator.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a complete BBQ evaluation protocol using GPT-4-turbo on over 16,000 disambiguated, three-choice examples, reporting accuracy across nine categories with eight-shot ICL. The stated WinoBias and Discrim-Eval settings remain unchanged; their newly disclosed refusal handling does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: New Appendix Table 6 tests Strategy III alone and combinations of Strategies I-III with Claude 2 on WinoBias, examining the contribution of explicit bias-inhibiting instructions. Earlier error decompositions, component ablations and counteraction-level sensitivity results are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or formal statistical tests. The added tables continue point-estimate reporting, and the existing human annotation counts remain unchanged.

E6.justification: BBQ Table 3 adds results showing DDP highest or tied in eight of nine categories, but below ICL on disability status: 95.76% versus 97.17%. Table 6 adds Claude 2 strategy-combination results, including a 1.01-point gap with all three strategies. All matched earlier numerical tables and Discrim-Eval plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds an independence-based fairness definition in Section 2.1 and Theorem 3.1 with a proof claiming complete conditional debiasing. It revises Strategy II's independence conditions, removes v1's separate downstream safeguard condition, extends the selection graph and discusses selection-induced violations of faithfulness. v1 contains no corresponding guarantee theorem.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly narrows the target from unbiased outputs or responses generally to unbiased decisions. Its conclusion newly claims complete bias removal when all three strategy objectives hold, strengthening v1's claims of principled and empirically effective debiasing. The black-box applicability and unification claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 reinterprets Strategy II as encouraging alternative fact-based reasoning, qualifies the practical attainability of the ideal independence objectives, and recommends fine-tuning first when weights and compute permit. Existing caveats about world knowledge, the Type II shortcut and residual Discrim-Eval bias remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses exclusion of WinoBias cases still refusing after more than three prompts, explains the balanced ICL examples, identifies GPT-4-turbo for BBQ, and describes regex or additional-query options for constructing base questions. Earlier temperature, model snapshots, human filtering and data/code disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds fairness-definition references and discussions of structured prompting, causal prompting, relation extraction and newer selection research, including Furniturewala et al. (2024), Zhang et al. (2024) and Zheng et al. (2024). Most earlier positioning remains; the selection-literature subsection largely relocates existing material.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and framework sections undergo extensive rewriting and reorganization. The title and method terminology change, a problem-setting subsection is introduced, and selection-related work and Discrim-Eval move into the appendices. These changes substantially reshape the narrative beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column main-text layout with single-column conference formatting, redesigns the introductory illustrations around a base-question workflow, condenses and redraws causal diagrams, adds two tables and an appendix contents page, and relocates the unchanged Discrim-Eval plots. Table sizing and captions also change.

improvement.justification: BBQ extends evidence to previously untested social categories, while the added ablation and refusal-handling disclosure improve assessability. However, the new central complete-debiasing guarantee has a proof gap: conditional independence from each decision parent separately does not establish the joint independence needed to infer independence of their combined output. The empirical and documentation gains coexist with this unsupported theoretical strengthening, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
